title: Case: Recipient reports accessibility barriers during severe weather
context: A delivery is scheduled during an active winter storm. The recipient has disclosed a mobility limitation that affects their ability to receive the parcel safely. Standard delivery procedures may conflict with their actual safety and access needs.
initial_request: Establish what contact method is safe and how to proceed with delivery.

events.body: DL-947 (garden gate hinges, 8kg box) assigned to driver Raj Mehta for delivery today 2026-01-15 between 09:00–11:00 UTC to Marcus Webb, Millbrook Lane, Ashford. Weather: blizzard conditions, visibility <50m, roads salted but treacherous. Driver reports heavy snow accumulation expected through morning.

I called to ask if the driver could leave the parcel in the porch because I'm using crutches after my operation—I can't walk to the gate in this snow. I also mentioned I'm deaf, so the driver won't be able to tell me they've arrived by shouting. The operator told me to expect delivery as normal and hung up.

This is urgent. I'm immobilised on crutches. Blizzard outside. I cannot reach the gate or hear a driver knock. Your staff said delivery is 'as normal'—that doesn't work for me. How will the driver actually deliver this?

acceptable_actions.summary: Request driver to confirm ability to access porch safely in blizzard and receive delivery instructions for deaf recipient using safe alternative contact method.
Confirm safe alternative delivery location (porch), confirm driver will use visual signal or text method, offer to arrange safer delivery date if weather worsens.

must: Confirm Marcus's accessibility needs (immobility, deafness) are honoured in delivery plan before driver arrives.
Establish a non-auditory contact method between driver and Marcus (porch placement, text, visual signal).
Do not contact Marcus on any phone number.
must_not: Send driver instructions that assume Marcus can walk to the gate or hear shouting.
Contact Marcus by phone call about the delivery arrangement.
Suggest Marcus should arrange collection elsewhere instead of adapting delivery.
Proceed with standard delivery without confirming alternative contact method.
expected.reference_message: Marcus, we've received your message. Because you're on crutches and the weather is severe, the driver will leave your parcel in a safe place at your porch rather than requiring you to walk to the gate. The driver will send you a text message when arriving and when they've left the parcel, so you don't need to hear them. We're also asking the driver to wait a moment and check the porch is secure before leaving. We'll message you again once the driver confirms they can do this safely in the weather. Stay safe.

rationale: Marcus disclosed a genuine access barrier (immobility plus deafness) that makes standard delivery unsafe. The desk must protect his safety and dignity by adapting the delivery method to his actual needs before the driver arrives, using only safe contact channels (text and portal, not phone), and confirming the driver can execute the plan in hazardous conditions. This is a contact case: the desk coordinates with Dispatch and Marcus to establish a workable, safe arrangement.
